newsitem.title: USA: CBOT July soybeans up sharply on supply worries.
newsitem.headline: CBOT July soybeans up sharply on supply worries.

text.p: Thursday's USDA stocks data showing tight supplies of nearby soybeans and firmness in cash markets pushed CBOT July sharply higher early Friday, traders said.
New crop contract months were also up, but gains in those contracts were limited by warm sunny, weather in much of the U.S. Midwest, conducive to new-crop development, traders said.

The National Oilseed Processors Association Thursday said U.S. soybean crushings during the week ended June 11 totaled 25.378 million bushels. That figured landed near the high end of a range of estimates from 24.6 million to 25.6 million bushels.
Soybean processors were still bidding aggressively for soybeans in U.S. cash markets, which also helped to move July higher, traders said.
In early trade, Rosenthal Collins bought two million bushels July and Tenco bought 500,000 bushels July. Locals were also seen as buyers on the open, traders said.
At 0937 CDT, July was up 8-1/2 cents per bushel at $8.50, and other months were up 1-3/4 to 6-1/2.
